findings.text: follow-on: _family_verdict pairs the two arms on lint_after and batches_run alone -- it reads neither code.git_head nor code.tree_digest_imas_codex nor harmonize_summary.halted -- so the fresh-code Jev arm this node lands is compared against the heuristic record at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab/current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport-heuristic.json, whose code.git_head is 5cf53a7b6dbc546eaff940398fa0c5e88f9e35b1 and whose harmonize_summary.halted is true. Both arms read batches_run 2, so like_for_like is true, lint_after 6 < 12 yields verdict jev-fewer, and _score_check reports passes true because its admissibility test only requires completeness 'full' -- reached by a halted arm whose batches_run equals batches_total. The adoption rule at selection.json then reads fewer findings with no lower score and would adopt the anchor from a comparison of a repaired-code arm against an unfixed-code arm. The landed record makes this reachable rather than causing it; the family verdict is another node's deliverable.

follow-on: the state paragraph reads 'the family no longer halted, and it stamped as harmonized', but the record it describes carries harmonize_receipts[0].harmonized false beside top-level stamped is true. The two mean different things -- plan_family_applies sets 'harmonized' from the plan-time decision (imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:1275), which is 'apply' for a family that still needs harmonizing, while the apply's finalize block sets 'stamped' true (imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:1526) after re-planning confirms zero remaining calls -- so no number is wrong, but a reader who follows the prose to the record finds the word 'harmonized' false there.
